overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 2
overview.text: In this lesson, students work on recursive formulas, building on the ideas that were introduced in Module 1, Lessons 26 and 27 (i.e., the double and add 5 game).
outcomes: Students write recursive and explicit formulas for sequences.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Core Mathematical Modeling for Recursive Formulas for Sequences
guidedExercises.problem: Classwork Opening (2 minutes) Remind students of their previous experiences with sequences. In Lesson 1, we worked on writing explicit formulas for sequences. Explicit formulas relate each term in a sequence directly to its placement in the sequence. This type of formula allows us to jump to any term of the sequence by simply replacing n with a specific number and evaluating the expression that describes the nth term of the sequence. exitTicket.title: Lesson 2 Exit Ticket: Recursive Formulas for Sequences
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

Consider the sequence following a minus 8 pattern: 9, 1, -7, -15, ….

Write an explicit formula for the sequence.

Write a recursive formula for the sequence.

Find the 38th term of the sequence.

Consider the sequence given by the formula a(n+1)=5a(n) and a(1)=2 for n≥1.

Explain what the formula means.

List the first five terms of the sequence.
exitTicket.solution:
Consider the sequence following a minus 8 pattern: 9, 1, -7, -15, ….

Write an explicit formula for the sequence.

f(n)=9-8(n-1) for n≥1

Write a recursive formula for the sequence.

f(n+1)=f(n)-8 and f(1)=9 for n≥1

Find the 38th term of the sequence.

f(38)=9-8(37)=-287

Consider the sequence given by the formula a(n+1)=5a(n) and a(1)=2 for n≥1.

Explain what the formula means.

The first term of the sequence is 2. Each subsequent term of the sequence is found by multiplying the previous term by 5.

List the first five terms of the sequence.

2, 10, 50, 250, 1250
